newsitem.title: JAPAN: TOCOM precious metals mostly up on strong dollar.
newsitem.headline: TOCOM precious metals mostly up on strong dollar.

text.p: Yen-based Tokyo precious metals futures ended firmer except for silver in moderate trade on Tuesday as the dollar rose vs the yen, Japanese traders said.
Gold futures ranged from one yen to 11 yen per gram higher. Benchmark June gold was up five yen at 1,226 yen.

"In gold futures, private investors were slightly on the buying side on seeing the dollar's rise, while activity in the bullion market was lacklustre due to holidays in the Hong Kong market," a trading house trader said.
Spot gold was quoted at $333.50/334.00 at 0725 GMT, against $333.70/334.20 in New York on Monday.
The focus in the gold market is on the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings on Tuesday and Wednesday.

"Spot gold has been at rock-bottom levels. As overseas funds built their shorts at an average $343.00 per ounce, they could cover their shorts if the FOMC leaves interest rates unchanged, as is widely expected," the trader said.

Platinum group metals (PGM) maintained firmer levels for most of the day. Although Japanese traders expected Russian PGM shipments to arrive in early July, tightness in the physical market after a six-month suspension of Russian sales would not be eased soon, the traders said.

"Japanese end-users have refrained from buying palladium, loathing high and volatile prices, which caused their stock levels to become low. Even after Russia resumes one-month contracted sales to Japan, the tightness will be unchanged," a PGM trader said. Platinum futures ranged from flat to 27 yen per gram higher. Benchmark June was up two yen at 1,353 yen.
Palladium futures ranged from eight yen to 18 yen per gram firmer, with benchmark June ending up 16 yen at 503 yen.
Silver futures were weaker following easier spot silver prices. Benchmark June silver was off 0.7 yen per 10 grams at 174.1 yen. --Tokyo Commodities Desk, +81-3-3432-7431
